finding:
⛔⛔ THE HEADLINE IS NOT THE THREE BLOCKERS — IT IS THAT TWO OF THEM WERE WRITTEN BY ROUND 26's OWN REPAIR COMMIT, AND THAT IS NOW PROVEN RATHER THAN SUSPECTED. `git log -S` on both offending strings against the journal article returns exactly two commits each: a294fee68 (round 26) introduced them, fade4a548 (round 27) removed them. The third blocker was not a paper defect at all — an unpublished Zenodo DOI, an outside-world state no review round could clear. ★ SO ZERO OF ROUND 27's BLOCKERS WERE PRE-EXISTING DEFECTS THE EARLIER ROUNDS MISSED. The paper is not decaying and the seats are not inventing work to fill a quota; the loop is breaking the paper with its own fixes. This is paper-hardening §8a's diagnosis with evidence attached, and it matches the skill's own record for round 24 (six of seven blockers were prior repairs).
⛔⛔ AND THE BAR MAKES IT NON-TERMINATING, WHICH IS THE STRUCTURAL HALF. clause_1 requires zero blockers ON THE COMMIT BEING POSTED. Any round that finds something produces repairs, which produce a new commit, which requires a new round. If a round's repairs reliably introduce a defect — and across rounds 24 and 27 they do — the loop cannot converge by construction. Twenty-seven rounds on a six-page paper is that fact, not bad luck.
★ THE MECHANISM, STATED SO IT CAN BE FIXED: a round both FINDS defects and CHANGES the paper, in one step. Five blind seats read 3,800 words; the four-word replacement that goes in afterwards is read by nobody until the next round. Round 26's error was visible in four words against one JSON field.
⭐ SECOND FINDING, AND IT IS trimcrae's: the loop had a standing grant to publish Zenodo depositions since 2026-08-30 and this cycle did not know it, because autonomy-state.json still asserts 'the Zenodo publish is still his by hand'. Filed as AUT-PD-196.
⭐ THIRD, MEASURED WHEN HE ASKED WHY PREFLIGHT WAS SLOW: the DEFAULT commit gate has a ~20x regression. `continuity.py --check` costs 24.6 s — cProfile attributes 28.5 s of 28.5 s to handoff.terminal_ids -> stuck_clock.ledger_versions, which makes 1,089 subprocess git calls (21.8 s, 22,477 select.poll waits) and is recomputed THREE times per invocation because nothing memoises it. 69 tests call it. The pure-logic step therefore runs 12-15 min on every tier against a documented 39.3 s, while PREFLIGHT_FULL's whole modalities suite is 7m33s. The expensive tier is the cheap part.
